department: Department of Environmental and Interdisciplinary Sciences (College of Science, Engineering and Technology)

deadline.value: The Ph.D. catalog page and Graduate School HTML admission pages state that deadlines vary by program and link to a PDF deadline table not extractable on this system; contact graduateadmissions@tsu.edu.

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists for Environmental Toxicology; ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Pre-admission supervisor agreement is not required; admission is recommended by the admissions committee and enrolled graduate students are assigned advisors by their department.
supervisor.quote: All graduate students are assigned advisors by their department.

also.quote: To be considered, the applicant must have earned the master’s degree in an appropriate field of the natural sciences or in an equivalent discipline acceptable to the admissions committee.

funding.value: The Graduate School provides tuition fellowships for a limited number of students nominated by their programs to work as teaching or research assistants.
funding.quote: The Graduate School provides tuition fellowships for a limited number of students nominated by their programs to work as teaching or research assistants.

entry_route.value: A master's degree in an appropriate natural sciences field (3.3 graduate GPA) is normally required; exceptional applicants without a master's may receive probationary admission requiring 18 master's-level credits.
entry_route.quote: To be considered, the applicant must have earned the master’s degree in an appropriate field of the natural sciences or in an equivalent discipline acceptable to the admissions committee. Exceptional applicants without a master’s degree may be granted a probationary admission but will be required to complete a total of eighteen (18) credit hours of coursework at the master’s level in biology, chemistry, and/or the Environmental Toxicology Program as approved by the department.

notes: Environmental Toxicology, Ph.D. (60 credit hours above M.S.) spans toxicology, environmental science, geology, GIS, remote sensing, risk assessment, and epidemiology. Requires GRE General and 3 letters of recommendation. Texas Southern University's Ph.D. in Urban Planning and Environmental Policy (School of Public Affairs) is excluded as an urban planning/public policy program.
name: Environmental Toxicology, Doctor of Philosophy
